A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RainbowPO research, with matching authors, framework and principal experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original Llama3-8B-Instruct fine-tuning experiments, component ablations and AlpacaEval2 comparisons in Tables 2–6.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, with additional training-epoch results and a training-loss curve in Appendix E.3, Table 13 and Figure 2.

M1.justification: RainbowPO retains length normalization, reference-policy mixing and contextual scaling. The explicit mixing loss, v1 Equation 11 and v2 Equation 14, and RS+ Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Expanded component formulas and tuning explanations do not establish an altered algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use UltraFeedback prompts with generated preference pairs scored by ArmoRM, and evaluate instruction following on the same 805 AlpacaEval2 prompts. The added epoch study retains this coverage; chain-of-thought and noisy-preference research are discussed only as future directions.

E2.justification: Table 5 retains DPO, IPO, KTO, CPO, ORPO and SimPO; Table 6 retains DPO and SimPO. Expanded appendix descriptions and the Mallows-DPO/MallowsPO renaming do not add evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix E.3 adds a controlled comparison of one, two, three and four training epochs, holding other hyperparameters at the three-epoch optimum. This differs from the retained, separately tuned one- and three-epoch comparisons. Newly specified decoding settings document existing evaluation rather than establish a protocol revision.

E4.justification: Table 13 and Figure 2 add training-duration sensitivity analysis, examining whether additional epochs improve evaluation scores as training loss decreases. Existing component ablations and margin, mixing-coefficient and rejection-sampling temperature analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same sigma-column reporting format, including for the added epoch results. No new seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are documented; numerical uncertainty changes in Table 4 are result updates.

E6.justification: Table 4 revises the no-contextual-scaling row: GPT4 LC WR/WR changes from 48.40/44.57 to 48.52/45.88, with corresponding Llama3-judge and response-length updates. New Table 13 reports LC WR of 46.36, 50.88 and 50.61 for one, two and four epochs under fixed hyperparameters. Tables 2, 3, 5 and 6 retain their numerical results, including RainbowPO's 51.66 LC WR.

T1.justification: V2 removes v1 Equation 12, the convexity-based bound relating the mixed-reference loss to LN-DPO and SimPO losses, and changes the stated GPO link function from log-sigmoid to negative log-sigmoid. The ORPO theorem and proof remain unchanged after relocation from Appendix B.1 to D.1; most added equations explain existing objectives.

C1.justification: The seven-component framework and headline 51.66 LC WR claim remain. The introduction now explicitly acknowledges reward-model access for constructing preferences. The conclusion drops its warm-up-adjustment claim and broadens the negative claim about rejection sampling and home advantage from combined use to individual use as well.

C2.justification: V2 explains how verbosity can inflate LLM-judge scores and how length-controlled evaluation mitigates that bias. It interprets the added epoch sweep as favoring three epochs and extends future-work discussion to chain-of-thought optimization and noisy preferences. Existing limitations concerning model and benchmark generality remain.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future code release; v2 states that code is available and supplies a repository link. V2 newly specifies evaluator templates, GPT4-turbo reference answers, generation settings of 4096 maximum new tokens, temperature 0.7 and top-p 0.1, and the gamma-then-alpha tuning order. Existing hyperparameter tables retain their values.

R1.justification: V2 adds Li et al. (2023), Dubois et al. (2024) and Wang et al. (2023) for evaluation background, plus Choi et al. (2024) and Chowdhury et al. (2024) for future directions. Song et al. (2024) and Zhou et al. (2024) disappear from the references. The central research positioning and prior-method taxonomy remain.

P1.justification: The exposition expands substantially: v1's two-sentence appendix explanation of XPO categories becomes nine method-specific subsections in v2 Appendix C. Section 3 gains explicit component explanations, Appendix E.1 adds an evaluation tutorial, and the appendices are reorganized. These are substantial explanatory and structural changes despite stable scientific foundations.

P2.justification: V2 adds the epoch-results Table 13 and training-loss Figure 2, repeats the component mapping as Table 9, and revises the notation table. Existing displays are relocated, captions and benchmark headings are clarified, and some best-score highlighting is corrected. Most table structures and Figure 1's plots remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves clarity and reproducibility through fuller component explanations, explicit decoding settings and code-access information. The controlled epoch ablation adds useful evidence, and revised Table 4 agrees with the corresponding stage in Table 3. These are limited gains with unchanged headline comparisons. The broader conclusion that rejection sampling provides no individual benefit overstates Table 2's retained small gains, tempering the improvement.
